summary: D. Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University (~1963–1970) and was a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College (1970–2000).
D. H. Gordon (1895–1961) was a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at Wellington College and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (~1914).

D. L. Narasimhachar (1906–1971) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore (~1925–1929). He held a post at the University of Mysore (~1932–1962) and taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

D. N. Dimri is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who completed doctoral studies at Doon University in 2014. Posts include Director of Publications at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2016) and researcher at the University of Pannonia (2018–2019).
D. N. Shukla worked in Indology, earning a D.Litt. at the University of Lucknow under supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer. He held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, attested in 1958.

D. Neil Schmid is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, Waseda University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where his doctoral supervisor was Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj (1954–1998) worked in Indology. He studied at Bangalore University (~1972–1977), later held a post there (~1978–1998), and taught Sheldon Pollock.
D. S. Subbaramaiya worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.
D. Srinivasachar worked in Indology. Attested between 1931 and 1933, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore.

Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) was a philosopher and linguist. Educated at the University of Oslo and Harvard under Willard Van Orman Quine, he taught at Harvard, the University of Oslo, and Stanford University (1968–2011), and taught Bimal Krishna Matilal.

Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her master's and doctoral degrees under Dorji Wangchuk at the University of Hamburg (~2004–2017) and has held positions at the University of British Columbia and the University of Leipzig.

Dagmar Wujastyk works in Indology, history, and archaeology. She served as a Principal Investigator at the University of Vienna in 2015 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Alberta in 2018.

Dagpo Rinpoche (born 1932) is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught David Seyfort Ruegg and Anne-Marie Blondeau, among others.

Taichi Tado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Positions include lecturer roles at Waseda University (attested 2020), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Daiei Kaneko (1881–1976) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Otani University (~1901–1904) under Manshi Kiyozawa, later holding posts at Toyo University and Otani University (~1916–1951), and founded Koho Gakuen.
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied and held a research student position at Ryukoku University, attested in 2006.

Daijaku Judith Kinst works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served as a faculty member at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

Daiju Sasaki (born 1977) specializes in Buddhist studies. Educated at Taisho University, he held posts there as a lecturer (attested 2015) and faculty member (attested 2026), and as a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Daijō Tokiwa (1870–1945) specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora, he was a professor at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and taught Enichi Ocho.

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Eihei-ji, and under Eko Hashimoto. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission, as interim abbot at San Francisco Zen Center, and founded Minnesota Zen Meditation Center.
